snippet.title: La mujer que MATÓ para Pablo Escobar: confesión real
snippet.description:
Hay ciudades que guardan secretos que ningún libro oficial se atreve a contar. Medellín fue una de ellas. En los años más oscuros del narcoterrorismo colombiano, mientras Pablo Escobar construía su imperio con sangre y pólvora, hubo mujeres que vivieron ese infierno desde adentro. Mujeres que mataron. Que sobrevivieron. Que perdieron todo. Y que hoy, décadas después, se atreven a hablar.

En este vídeo te contamos la historia de Amparo, alias 'La Negra', sicaria de Pablo Escobar y miembro activo del combo de los Prisco Lopera, una de las estructuras criminales más temidas de las comunas de Medellín. Un testimonio brutalmente honesto sobre cómo una niña criada entre armas, leche para borrar rastros de pólvora y rituales del crimen organizado terminó convirtiéndose en uno de los eslabones más letales del Cartel de Medellín.

Esta no es una historia de glorificación. Es una historia de verdad. La verdad de quien lo vivió en carne propia: el reclutamiento en las canchas de fútbol, la mirada de piedra de Escobar eligiendo a sus sicarios, la lealtad comprada con hambre y necesidad, y el precio brutal que se paga cuando se entra a ese mundo sin saber si algún día se podrá salir.

Descubrirás cómo Pablo Escobar reclutaba a jóvenes de las comunas del nororiente de Medellín, qué papel jugaron las mujeres dentro del narcotráfico colombiano, cómo funcionaba la cadena de obediencia dentro de los combos y por qué tantos muchachos y muchachas de barrios como Aranjuez, Popular y Santa Cruz no tuvieron otra opción que convertirse en parte de esa maquinaria de muerte.

Confesiones reales. Crimen organizado colombiano. Historia sin filtros.

snippet.title: Inside the Gemini Lounge: Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa’s Rise Into Mafia Horror (True Crime)
snippet.description:
It looked like a normal neighborhood bar in Flatlands, Brooklyn. A place where working men drank, locals talked, and nobody outside the life asked too many questions. But behind the doors of the Gemini Lounge, Roy DeMeo’s crew built one of the most terrifying murder machines in Mafia history — and Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa rose right in the middle of it.

They were young, close, and almost inseparable. To the streets, they became known as the Gemini Twins. But this was not a nickname built on loyalty alone. It was built inside a crew where stolen cars, drug money, fear, and murder all moved through the same Brooklyn pipeline.

By the late 1970s, Senter and Testa were no longer just kids around the crew. They were part of the core. Roy DeMeo had built an operation that made money fast and made witnesses disappear faster. The Gemini Lounge became the center of the world around them — a bar, a meeting place, a criminal headquarters, and for many people, the last address they would ever see.

What you will learn in this documentary:
How Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa grew up in Brooklyn and became known as the Gemini Twins
Why their friendship made them useful, dangerous, and trusted inside the DeMeo crew
How Roy DeMeo turned the Gemini Lounge into the center of his criminal empire
Why the DeMeo crew became one of the most feared crews in Gambino family history
How stolen cars, chop shops, narcotics, loansharking, and murder all fed the same machine
Why Chris Rosenberg, Henry Borelli, and Roy DeMeo helped shape the world Senter and Testa entered
How the Gemini Lounge became linked to one of the darkest reputations in New York Mafia history
Why the crew’s murder method terrified even other mobsters
How Senter and Testa rose from young associates to trusted killers
Why Paul Castellano and Nino Gaggi began seeing the DeMeo crew as both profitable and dangerous
How the murder of Roy DeMeo changed the future of the Gemini Twins
Why Senter and Testa moved from the Gambino orbit into the Lucchese family
How their 1989 convictions finally exposed the horror behind the Gemini Lounge

Key figures:
Anthony Senter, Joseph Testa, Roy DeMeo, Nino Gaggi, Paul Castellano, Chris Rosenberg, Henry Borelli, Joey Testa, Patrick Testa, Vito Arena, Dominick Montiglio, Frederick DiNome, Richard DiNome, Anthony “Gaspipe” Casso, Vic Amuso, John Gotti, Sammy Gravano, Gambino crime family, Lucchese crime family

Timeline:
1955 births of Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa in New York, early 1970s rise through Brooklyn street crime, 1974 Senter and Testa become connected to Roy DeMeo’s crew, mid-1970s the Gemini Lounge becomes the crew’s headquarters in Flatlands, 1975 to 1982 the DeMeo crew expands through auto theft, narcotics, loansharking, and murder, 1979 Dominick Ragucci is killed after being mistaken for a threat, 1980 Chris Rosenberg is murdered, January 10 1983 Roy DeMeo disappears, January 20 1983 DeMeo is found dead in the trunk of his Cadillac, 1984 federal racketeering charges begin closing in on the crew, 1986 first DeMeo crew convictions, 1989 Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa are convicted of racketeering and multiple murders, 1989 both men receive life sentences.

Why this story matters today:
The Gemini Lounge story matters because it shows the Mafia at its most terrifying. This was not the glamorous mob of suits, restaurants, and movie quotes. This was a crew built on speed, silence, fear, and routine violence. Anthony Senter and Joseph Testa rose inside a world where murder became part of business, where a neighborhood bar hid a killing operation, and where loyalty lasted only until someone became a risk. The Gemini Twins did not just join the horror of the DeMeo crew. They helped make the Gemini Lounge one of the darkest names in Mafia history.

If the Versailles Palace is renowned throughout the world, it is mainly for its fountains; each year, some 10 million visitors come to admire them. But how many actually know that they work thanks to 35 km of piping and 70,000 m3 of water? 

At the time, the Sun King did not accept anything less than greatly ambitious. Creative devices and ever more ingenious machines were necessary to pump water into all these fountains. How did these millions of cubic meters of water get the pressure necessary to make so much water flow? Where does Versailles’ water come from? How is it supplied and managed?
Embark with us on the waters of Versailles; this documentary takes you on a journey through its incredible underground maze of an engineering system.

snippet.title: The REAL REASON the FBI Couldn't Touch the Florida Godfather
snippet.description:
In the 1950s, he controlled the glamorous, neon-lit casinos of Havana. By the 1960s, he was secretly working with the CIA to assassinate a foreign dictator. And by the 1980s, he survived the most famous FBI undercover sting in history. This is the unbelievable true story of Santo Trafficante Jr., the Florida Godfather.

While New York mobsters chased headlines and ended up in prison, Trafficante built an empire in the shadows. He didn't use violence when a bribe would work. He didn't threaten the government; he partnered with them. In this episode of MAFIA TALKS, we break down how one quiet boss outsmarted Fidel Castro, the Kennedy administration, and the FBI's "Donnie Brasco" operation.

🔍 What you will learn in this documentary:

The brilliant mechanics of the "Bolita" numbers racket that built his fortune.

Step-by-step breakdown of how the Mafia skimmed millions from Batista’s Cuba.

The exact details of the CIA's top-secret "poison pill" plot against Fidel Castro.

Why the House Select Committee on Assassinations suspected him of killing JFK.

How he beat the FBI in federal court at the age of 71.

Key Figures: Santo Trafficante Jr., Meyer Lansky, Fidel Castro, Jack Ruby, Joe Pistone (Donnie Brasco).
Timeline: 1954 (Tampa Boss) - 1959 (Cuban Revolution) - 1987 (Death).

Why does this matter today? Trafficante's life proves that the line between organized crime and international politics is terrifyingly thin. He weaponized government secrets to ensure his own survival, creating a blueprint for the modern, insulated crime syndicate.

Esta es la historia del hombre que la poseía, que la vendió, y que jamás pudo pronunciar su propio nombre en voz alta después de hacerlo. Un campesino humilde, hijo de veterinario, que creció entre el olor a formol y creolina en Puerto Triunfo, y que soñaba con tener tanta tierra que necesitaría un helicóptero para verla completa. Nadie imaginaba que ese sueño lo llevaría directo al infierno.

En este episodio de Relato Mafioso te contamos la historia real y desconocida del hombre que le vendió la Hacienda Nápoles a Pablo Escobar: cómo llegó hasta allí, qué vio, qué escuchó y por qué lleva décadas viviendo con el peso de esa decisión. Una historia narrada desde adentro, con nombres, lugares y detalles que nunca habías escuchado.

Escobar no construyó su imperio de la nada. Necesitó tierra, espacio y silencio. Necesitó a alguien que conociera el Magdalena Medio como la palma de su mano. Y ese alguien existió. Firmó una escritura. Cobró en efectivo. Y desde ese día, nunca más volvió a dormir tranquilo.

Esta historia no es solo sobre el narcotráfico colombiano ni sobre el capo más buscado de la historia. Es sobre lo que le ocurre a un hombre común cuando la codicia, la necesidad y el miedo se cruzan en el mismo camino. snippet.title: Los Zetas: El Ejército que el Estado Creó Sin Saberlo
snippet.description:
Había una organización que no nació en las sombras del crimen, sino en el corazón del propio Estado mexicano. Hombres entrenados por el ejército, instruidos por asesores estadounidenses e israelíes, seleccionados entre los mejores soldados de su generación. Hombres que un día decidieron cambiar el uniforme por algo mucho más lucrativo y mucho más oscuro. Esta es la historia de Los Zetas, el cartel más brutal, más disciplinado y más temido que ha existido en la historia del crimen organizado latinoamericano.

En este vídeo reconstruimos desde sus orígenes militares hasta su expansión imparable por México y Centroamérica. Analizamos cómo un grupo de treinta y cinco desertores del Grupo Aeromóvil de Fuerzas Especiales transformó para siempre el narcotráfico mexicano, introduciendo tácticas de guerra real en el mundo criminal. Entenderás cómo Los Zetas industrializaron la violencia, capturaron instituciones enteras y sembraron el terror en decenas de estados durante más de una década.

Desde la figura de Arturo Guzmán Decena, el Z-Uno que lo inició todo, hasta la traición al Cartel del Golfo que los convertiría en una potencia independiente, cada capítulo de esta historia supera en brutalidad y complejidad a cualquier serie de televisión. Y lo más perturbador es que todo es real. Cada dato está documentado. Cada nombre existió. Cada crimen ocurrió.

Esta es la historia del ejército privado más letal que el narcotráfico haya creado jamás. La historia de cómo el Estado pagó sin saberlo por su propio enemigo más peligroso. La historia que, cuando termines de escuchar, cambiará para siempre tu manera de entender el crimen organizado en México y en toda América Latina.

snippet.title: The Mafia Footage No One Thought Existed
snippet.description:
Miami, 1929. Charles “Lucky” Luciano and Frank Costello appear in a rare home reel long attributed to Al Capone’s private archive. In late Prohibition Miami, resorts often served as neutral ground: sunshine for cover, phone calls for business. Their partnership ran on complementary strengths: Luciano shaped the new structure that became the Five Families and the Commission in 1931, while Costello supplied political access, union contacts, and the gambling revenue that kept the machine smooth. They stood together through the Castellammarese War and the break with the old guard, choosing profit over vendetta. After Luciano’s 1936 conviction and his 1946 deportation, Costello kept the family steady as acting boss, protecting his friend’s interests from New York to Havana. The film reads casual, yet it captures a working friendship that helped turn scattered crews into a national syndicate. The Capone attribution is debated among collectors; the influence of the men on screen is not.

snippet.title: The Real Sonny Black Was the Most Dangerous Man in Donnie Brasco
snippet.description:
On August 17, 1981, a 51-year-old Bonanno captain walked into a Brooklyn basement and never walked out. He took his jewelry off before he left. He left his keys with the bartender. He already knew what was waiting for him at the bottom of those stairs.

Everybody remembers Donnie Brasco. The 6-year FBI undercover. The 200+ indictments. The Johnny Depp movie. Almost nobody remembers the man who actually paid for it. This is the full untold story of Dominick “Sonny Black” Napolitano, the Bonanno caporegime who vouched for Joseph Pistone, nearly inducted him into the family, and was executed for treason he never knew he committed.

In this documentary you will learn:
 • How Sonny Black rose from Greenpoint to caporegime of one of Brooklyn’s most active crews
 • The exact moment Joe Pistone was inserted into the Bonanno family in 1976
 • How the Three Capos Murder of May 5, 1981 set the stage for Sonny’s death
 • The 19 days Sonny lived knowing he was already a dead man
 • The Bruno Indelicato hit contract that forced the FBI to pull Pistone
 • What really happened in the basement on East 58th Street on August 17, 1981
 • Why his hands were severed and his body dumped in a Staten Island creek
 • How Joseph Massino, who killed Sonny, became the biggest mob rat in history

Key figures: 
Dominick “Sonny Black” Napolitano, Joseph D. Pistone (Donnie Brasco), Benjamin “Lefty” Ruggiero, Joseph “Big Joey” Massino, Frank Lino, Alphonse “Sonny Red” Indelicato, Philip Rastelli.

Timeline: 
- 1976 Pistone infiltrates 
- 1980 Sonny prepares to induct Brasco 
- May 5, 1981 Three Capos Murder 
- July 28, 1981 FBI reveals identity 
- August 17, 1981 Sonny executed 
- August 12, 1982 body found.

This story matters because it exposes the Mafia myth. The “code of honor” did not protect Sonny Black. It killed him for following it perfectly. In an era where loyalty is sold as a virtue, his story is the receipt.

snippet.title: La Mafia Israelí: Sangre, Poder e Impunidad
snippet.description:
El imperio criminal más poderoso que ningún gobierno se atrevió a tocar durante décadas. La mafia israelí no es un mito ni una leyenda urbana: fue una máquina de crimen organizado que controló el 75% del éxtasis en Estados Unidos, blanqueó miles de millones de dólares a través del comercio de diamantes y construyó una industria del fraude capaz de robar 10.000 millones de dólares al año a víctimas de todo el mundo.

En este vídeo te contamos la historia completa de cómo las redes criminales israelíes pasaron de los barrios marginales de Tel Aviv a convertirse en una fuerza global del crimen organizado. Desde los orígenes en las comunidades mizrajíes discriminadas de los años 50, hasta las brutales guerras de territorio que sembraron el caos en las calles israelíes con coches bomba, misiles antitanque y sicarios importados de Europa del Este.

Conocerás a los grandes capos que construyeron este imperio: Yitzhak Abergil, estratega frío que leyó a Nietzsche en prisión antes de levantar su organización criminal. Zeve Rosenstein, el hombre que sobrevivió a más atentados que ningún otro mafioso. Los hermanos Alperon, doce hijos de una familia egipcia convertidos en una máquina de extorsión. Y la oleada de crimen organizado ruso que llegó con la caída de la Unión Soviética y blanqueó hasta 10.000 millones de dólares sin que nadie pusiera freno.

Una historia de pobreza, poder, impunidad y sangre. Una historia que el Estado de Israel quiso enterrar durante décadas bajo la mentira de que el crimen organizado no existía en la tierra prometida. Hasta que una bomba en el centro de Tel Aviv lo hizo imposible de ignorar.

Dieses Video erzählt die tragische Geschichte von Ingrid Bergman: ihren Aufstieg in Hollywood, ihren weltweiten Ruhm, den Skandal um Roberto Rossellini, ihre öffentliche Verurteilung in Amerika und ihren langen, schmerzhaften Weg zurück.

Im Mittelpunkt steht nicht nur die Filmikone aus Casablanca, sondern der Mensch hinter dem Mythos. Es geht um die junge Frau aus Stockholm, um ihren Durchbruch in Hollywood, um die Rolle, die ihr die Studios zuschrieben, und um den Moment, in dem sie sich entschied, nicht länger nur ein Bild zu sein, das andere von ihr sehen wollten. Genau dieser Schritt brachte ihr Bewunderung, aber auch gesellschaftliche Ächtung und berufliches Exil ein.

– wie Ingrid Bergman in Hollywood zur Ikone wurde
– warum ihre Beziehung zu Roberto Rossellini einen Skandal auslöste
– wie weit Amerika in ihrer öffentlichen Verurteilung ging
– weshalb ihre Karriere in Europa künstlerisch sogar mutiger wurde

snippet.title: The Real Neil McCauley Was the Most Dangerous Criminal Behind Heat Movie
snippet.description:
On March 25, 1964, in a pouring Chicago rainstorm, a professional thief named Neil McCauley walked out of a National Tea grocery store at 4720 South Cicero Avenue with $13,137 in stolen cash. Nine detectives were waiting. Hundreds of rounds were fired. And the man who finally caught McCauley in a residential gangway and shot him 6 times had once bought him a cup of coffee at a deli on North Clark Street.

That cop’s name was Chuck Adamson. 32 years later, he’d tell that story to a young filmmaker named Michael Mann. The result was HEAT (1995).
In this documentary, we trace the real 3-year cat-and-mouse pursuit between Chicago detective Chuck Adamson and career criminal Neil McCauley — the events Michael Mann adapted almost word-for-word into the most iconic crime film of the 1990s.

🔎 What you’ll learn:
 • Who Neil McCauley really was — 25 years in prison, 8 inside Alcatraz, 4 in solitary
 • The real “diner scene” — the actual 1963 conversation at the Belden Corned Beef Center, 2315 N. Clark Street
 • The aborted Wieboldt’s heist that inspired the abandoned-score scene in HEAT
 • The full 1964 National Tea shootout — every shot, every fallen crew member
 • How Adamson became a TV writer for Miami Vice and Crime Story
 • Why Michael Mann spent 16 years turning this case into a film

📅 Key timeline:
 • 1914 — McCauley born in Polk, Iowa
 • 1962 — Released from federal prison after 25 years
 • 1963 — Coffee meeting with Adamson in Lincoln Park
 • March 25, 1964 — The shootout that ended it all
 • 1979 — Mann writes first HEAT script
 • 1995 — HEAT releases in theaters
 • 2008 — Adamson dies; Mann dedicates Public Enemies to him

This isn’t movie myth. Every quote, every address, every bullet — documented.

snippet.title: Clark Gable: Die tragische Geschichte seiner 2 Kinder
snippet.description:
Clark Gable war der König von Hollywood – doch von seinen beiden Kindern hat er keines wirklich gekannt. Das ist die wahre Familiengeschichte hinter der Legende.

Als Clark Gable 1960 starb, hinterließ er weit mehr als „Vom Winde verweht" und fünf Ehen. Er hinterließ ein jahrzehntelang gehütetes Geheimnis: eine Tochter, Judy Lewis, gezeugt mit Loretta Young während der Dreharbeiten zu „Ruf der Wildnis" – versteckt in einem Waisenhaus, als angebliche Adoptivtochter zurückgeholt und als Kind operiert, damit sie ihrem berühmten Vater nicht zu ähnlich sah. Erst mit 31 erfuhr sie die Wahrheit. Und während Judy mit diesem Geheimnis lebte, kam vier Monate nach Gables Tod sein Sohn John Clark Gable zur Welt – ein Junge, der den größten Namen Hollywoods trug und seinen Vater nie traf. Diese Doku erzählt das Schicksal beider Kinder, ihrer Mutter Loretta Young und der dritten Generation, die denselben Namen weitertrug.

snippet.title: The Jewish Mafia’s Deadliest Hitmen of All Time
snippet.description:
They did not wear crowns. They did not sit in marble mansions. They waited in candy stores, pool halls, tenements, and Brooklyn corners until the phone rang. Then somebody disappeared. This is the story of the Jewish hitmen who helped make New York fear the mob.

In the 1930s, the American Mafia was becoming more organized, more national, and more ruthless. Lucky Luciano wanted structure. Meyer Lansky understood money. Louis “Lepke” Buchalter understood labor rackets. Albert Anastasia understood murder. Together, their world created one of the most terrifying enforcement machines in American criminal history: Murder, Inc.

Its killers came from the hardest streets of Brooklyn and Manhattan. Many were Jewish. Some were Italian. All were useful because they did what bosses could not do openly. They killed for money, loyalty, fear, and silence. From Brownsville to the Lower East Side, from union rackets to waterfront disputes, from witnesses to rivals, Murder, Inc. became the shadow army of the National Crime Syndicate.

What you will learn in this documentary:
How Jewish gangsters became essential to the rise of New York organized crime
Why Brownsville, East New York, Ocean Hill, and the Lower East Side produced some of the most feared killers in America
How Meyer Lansky, Bugsy Siegel, and Lucky Luciano helped build a multi-ethnic crime alliance
Why Louis “Lepke” Buchalter needed a murder squad to protect his labor rackets
How Albert Anastasia became tied to the enforcement arm of the Mafia
Why Rosie Gold’s candy store became one of the most infamous meeting spots in mob history
How Abe “Kid Twist” Reles rose from street thug to Murder, Inc. executioner
Why Harry “Pittsburgh Phil” Strauss became one of the crew’s most feared killers
How Buggsy Goldstein, Happy Maione, Frank Abbandando, and others turned contract killing into routine business
Why witnesses, informants, union enemies, and loose ends became targets
How Thomas Dewey and Brooklyn prosecutors finally cracked the murder machine
Why Abe Reles became the canary who sang — then fell from a window before he could testify against Albert Anastasia

snippet.title: Why Pablo Escobar Hunted His Secret Son for 30 Years
snippet.description:
For nearly thirty years, the world believed Pablo Escobar had two children. Juan Pablo and Manuela. The kids he loved.

But in 1965, on the outskirts of Bogotá, a baby survived a shootout that killed his fourteen-year-old mother. That baby was Roberto Sendoya Escobar: Pablo's firstborn son. He was raised in secret by a British MI6 officer. He grew up under bodyguards, in armoured cars, with another name.

And for years, his biological father tried to take him back by force.

This is the story almost no one tells.

snippet.title: Joey Merlino Wanted Philly — Then His Best Friend Took the Bullets
snippet.description:
He was young, loud, fearless, and nothing like the old bosses who ruled Philadelphia before him. Joey Merlino did not quietly inherit the Philly mob. He fought for it. And when he rose from South Philly street kid to the most famous gangster in the city, the Mafia turned Philadelphia into a war zone.

After Nicky Scarfo was sent away, the Philadelphia crime family was broken, paranoid, and leaderless. New York wanted order. The old guard wanted control. John Stanfa was supposed to bring discipline back to the family. But Joey Merlino and his young crew had other plans. They did not want to wait. They did not want permission. They wanted the city.

By 1993, the war was no longer hidden. Cars were sprayed with bullets. Hitmen missed targets. Friends were killed in daylight. Stanfa’s men tried to erase Merlino, but the bullets only made his legend bigger. When Michael Ciancaglini died beside him and Merlino survived with four wounds, South Philly understood the message: the new generation was not backing down.

What you will learn in this documentary:
How Joey Merlino rose from South Philadelphia streets to the top of the Philly mob
Why Nicky Scarfo’s downfall left the family broken and exposed
How John Stanfa became the old-guard boss backed by outside power
Why Merlino and the young Turks refused to accept Stanfa’s rule
How a local power struggle turned into one of the bloodiest mob wars of the 1990s
The 1993 shooting that killed Michael Ciancaglini and nearly killed Merlino
Why Merlino surviving the ambush changed his reputation overnight
How Stanfa’s crew used bombs, drive-by shootings, and street hits to hold power
Why Merlino’s side fought back with the same brutality
How Ralph Natale became boss while Merlino became the real power behind the family
Why the FBI used informants, wiretaps, and surveillance to break the war open
How Ron Previte’s cooperation helped expose the modern Philly mob
Why Merlino became known as the John Gotti of Passyunk Avenue
How the war ended with Stanfa in prison and Merlino standing on top

Why this story matters today:
Joey Merlino’s story matters because it shows the last violent transformation of the Philadelphia Mafia. The old world of Angelo Bruno and Nicky Scarfo was already collapsing, but Merlino’s rise turned that collapse into open war. He brought youth, publicity, attitude, and street-level aggression into a family that was already bleeding from betrayal and prison sentences. When Merlino took over Philly, he did not just become another mob boss. He became the symbol of a new era where the Mafia was weaker, louder, more reckless, and still deadly enough to turn the city into a battlefield.

snippet.title: VITO GENOVESE - Der Aufstieg und Fall des Anführers der amerikanischen Mafia.
snippet.description:
Vito Genovese gehört zu den einflussreichsten und zugleich umstrittensten Figuren der amerikanischen Unterwelt des zwanzigsten Jahrhunderts. Geboren in der Nähe von Neapel, wanderte er als Jugendlicher in die Vereinigten Staaten aus und stieg im Umfeld der italienisch-amerikanischen Mafia schnell auf. In den Jahren der Prohibition nutzte er illegale Geschäfte, Machtkämpfe und strategische Allianzen, um zu einer zentralen Figur innerhalb der Cosa Nostra zu werden.

Diese Dokumentation verfolgt seinen Weg vom Einwanderer in New York bis zum mächtigen Boss einer der fünf Mafiafamilien. Die Geschichte umfasst den Castellammarese-Krieg, die Entstehung der „Kommission“, interne Machtkämpfe innerhalb der Mafia sowie Ereignisse wie den Anschlag auf Frank Costello, die Ermordung von Albert Anastasia und das berüchtigte Treffen von Apalachin.

Doch Genoveses Aufstieg brachte auch immer stärkere Aufmerksamkeit der Behörden mit sich. snippet.title: How Matta Ballesteros Built a Crack Empire (And How He Lost It) | Our History
snippet.description:
Born in Honduras, Juan Ramon Matta Ballesteros worked his way up from penniless street child, to become one of the richest cocaine smugglers in history and one of the most wanted men in America. Forging links with the Cali, Medellin and Guadalajara cartels, Ballesteros masterminded a supply route into the US, which fed much of the cocaine and crack epidemic of the 70s and 80s. But when Ballesteros was implicated in the murder of a DEA agent, Mike Vigil was appointed to hunt him down. He would stop at nothing until Ballesteros was behind bars.
